ExampleDefinition.ToolTipDescription: Demonstrates a real-time animated Uniform Vector Field chart driven by four interfering radial wave sources, using UniformVectorFieldDataSeries on a resizable grid.
ExampleDefinition.Description:
This example demonstrates a real-time [b]Uniform Vector Field Chart[/b] - a grid of arrows, each drawn as a stem line with an arrowhead indicating direction and magnitude, animated at up to ~50 fps.
The chart uses [b]VectorFieldRenderableSeries[/b] and [b]UniformVectorFieldDataSeries[/b]. The field is computed from four superimposed radial wave sources that produce smooth interference patterns across a 70x46 grid spanning [-15, 15] x [-10, 10].
Each frame the displacement values are rewritten directly into the backing 2D arrays and [b]InvalidateParentSurface[/b] is called - no DataSeries reallocation occurs. [b]FieldDataDistributionArgs[/b] supplies pre-known data extents so SciChart can skip the O(N) range scan on every update.
Two update modes are available via the toolbar: - [b]Normal[/b] - a background thread-pool timer fires every 20 ms (~50 fps); the rendering handler invalidates the chart only when new data is ready, keeping the UI thread free between updates. - [b]Performance[/b] - the data update runs directly inside CompositionTarget.Rendering every frame for maximum throughput, with a FPS overlay shown.
[b]Features demonstrated[/b]
- UniformVectorFieldDataSeries on a resizable grid (adjustable via slider while stopped) - Real-time in-place DX/DY update without reallocating the DataSeries - FieldDataDistributionArgs to bypass per-frame O(N) range scans - Color mapping by magnitude or by direction via HeatmapColorPalette - Three arrow length modes: DataUnits, MagnitudePixels, FixedPixels - Normal and Performance update modes with optional FPS overlay
